source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
A detailed cost breakdown for growing red corn (survey-based, average across sampled provinces) shows total production cost of about 19,773,717 riel per household on an average landholding of 3.68 hectares, working out to about 5,373,293 riel per hectare per season. The cost categories and their share of total cost were:

1. Seed cost: 1,335,686 riel (7% of total).
2. Land cost (own-land opportunity cost and rented land combined): 1,842,242 riel (9%) -- split between rented land (1,017,333 riel, 5%) and the amortized value/cost of using own land (824,909 riel, 4%).
3. Fertilizer and agrochemical use: 957,270 riel (5%) -- split between pre-planting fertilizer application (382,667 riel, 2%), post-planting fertilizer application (288,277 riel, 1.5%), and pesticide/herbicide use (286,325 riel, 1.5%).
4. Land preparation (plowing/tillage): 1,343,667 riel (7%) -- split between tractor-based land clearing (686,664 riel, 3%) and forming planting rows/ridges (657,003 riel, 3%).
5. Labor: 2,956,426 riel (15%, the single largest operational-labor category) -- split between planting/sowing labor (414,336 riel, 2%), weeding labor (589,820 riel, 3%), harvest labor (1,399,068 riel, 7%), and equipment/tool costs (553,203 riel, 3%).
6. Transport and marketing to sell the crop: 431,874 riel (2%).
7. Land cost/rent counted as a single lump seasonal or annual charge: 3,641,725 riel (18%, the single largest cost category overall).
8. Miscellaneous other expenses: 165,222 riel (1%).

The combined weight of land-related costs (land preparation + land rent/opportunity cost, items 2, 4, and 7 above) makes land access and preparation the dominant cost driver in red-corn production, together exceeding a third of total production cost, ahead of labor and well ahead of seed or fertilizer costs.
